description:
A mutation reads the repository once instead of in three gated rounds, and the phase-to-phase coherence check goes with the phasing.

## Background

A changing mutation performs six capture rounds: two in a preflight session, three in the attempt session, and one at apply. The attempt rounds are an ad-hoc protocol in the command layer: a registry-only round, a round adding the event log and every indexed issue file, and a third re-reading all of it plus per-profile records, working-tree document paths, precheck prompts, and gate-run paths. An overlap-stability check gates each round against the one before it.

With publication comparing only the files it writes, the phasing has nothing left to certify. A mutation reads its base set in one pass, and a caller's named paths and listings join that same round. The apply-time round is already gone, and the preflight collapses to one round.

The first cut keeps reading every indexed issue, because dependency-graph derivation and hierarchy validation need the full issue set to detect cycles and transitive redundancy. That cost scales with issue count, which is what the latency target requires.

## Success Criteria

- [hard] REQ-01: A changing mutation performs one capture round in its attempt and one in its preflight, with no round gated by an overlap-stability check.
- [hard] REQ-02: No phase-one capture specification, phase-three specification, or overlap-stability check survives in the workspace.
- [hard] REQ-03: The capture's base specification reads the registries, the index, the event log, the indexed issue files, and the plan documents a transition rule consults; a caller's named paths and listings are added to that one round.
- [hard] REQ-04: Gate-run result capture joins the same round, with its own further rounds gone.
- [hard] REQ-05: A pure producer reading a path the capture did not discover still fails typed.
- [hard] REQ-06: Capture remains budget-bounded, with no whole-worktree recursion.
- [hard] REQ-07: The change removes more lines than it adds.

## Notes

The phase-two closure-change retry test loses its referent and goes with the phasing; the property that a changed closure discards and recaptures survives as a single-pass recapture.
title: Single-pass mutation capture
